Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided hearing reduction, facial numbness around the left ear/jaw, and intermittent tinnitus with occasional dizziness. No red-flag neurological or otological symptoms elicited. Telehealth GP advised urgent same-day face-to-face review to examine for suspected Bell’s palsy and exclude other causes.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness (3 weeks)
- Onset: gradual over 3 weeks.
- Location: left ear (hearing ↓), numbness over left peri-auricular jawline; constant at presentation.
- Associated: intermittent tinnitus and brief dizziness. No limb weakness, dysphasia, dysphagia, visual change, otalgia, otorrhoea, fever, or pruritus.
- Differential discussed: Bell’s palsy considered; other otological/neurological causes to be excluded with physical exam.
- Impact: limiting jockey training/work.

Issue 2: Past nasal polyps
- Intermittent; treated PRN with intranasal spray (name unknown, dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Currently asymptomatic.

Issue 3: History of labyrinthitis (remote, not current)
- No ongoing vertigo noted.

Medications:
- Intranasal spray for nasal polyps (name and dose/route/frequency not documented; used PRN).
- Rennie (calcium carbonate antacid) PRN; dose/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Latex (reaction details not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps.
- Previous episode of labyrinthitis (resolved).

Social History:
- Occupation: professional jockey; reduced activity due to symptoms.
- Living arrangements: initially stated “live alone”, later “live with partner” – conflict noted.
- No pets mentioned.
- Smoking and alcohol history not documented.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on screening tests or vaccinations.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals or physical exam performed.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day, face-to-face GP clinic appointment in Central London for:
  • Full neurological and cranial nerve examination.
  • Otoscopic examination.
  • Confirm or exclude Bell’s palsy and other differential diagnoses.
- Admin team to contact patient; patient instructed to phone support team within 5 minutes to schedule appointment today.
- Provide reassurance that condition appears non-life-threatening pending assessment.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vitals, physical exam findings, smoking/alcohol history, full medication list with doses, vaccination and screening status.
● Internal conflicts: patient first said “live alone,” later “live with my partner.”
● Transcript quality: clear audio with minimal background noise; minor pauses but overall adequate for documentation.
